questions.prompt: A Node request handler wraps its work in `storage.run({requestId}, callback)`. A timer created inside callback later reads `storage.getStore()`. What is the intended result?

choices.text: The context ends before the timer runs.
The timer reads whichever request most recently called run globally.
The store is serialized into the timer arguments by the runtime first.
That request context is available.

questions.explanation: AsyncLocalStorage propagates the store to asynchronous operations created within run. It does not use one global latest request or require explicit timer argument serialization.

sources.title: Asynchronous context tracking | Node.js v26.11.1 Documentation
sources.claim: AsyncLocalStorage.run propagates its store to async operations created inside the callback; an instance without a defaultValue returns undefined when no store is provided.

questions.prompt: A Node EventEmitter emits `error` without any error listener. Which behavior should its owner expect?

choices.text: The error is thrown.
The event is silently ignored.
The emitter automatically retries the previous event on the next tick.
The event is converted into a handled promise rejection automatically.

questions.explanation: error is special: without a listener the error is thrown and the process can exit. Normal events without listeners do not have that behavior.

sources.title: Events | Node.js v26.11.1 Documentation
sources.claim: EventEmitter listeners execute synchronously in registration order; an unhandled error event throws and may terminate the process.

questions.prompt: A Node service allocates and slices Buffers before returning data to clients. Which statements are accurate? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Buffer.slice creates a view sharing the original memory.
Buffer.slice always makes an independent copy of its bytes.
The Unsafe suffix changes bounds checking while still always clearing memory.
Buffer.alloc produces a zero-filled allocation.
Buffer.allocUnsafe requires every exposed byte to be initialized first.

questions.explanation: A is correct: writing the slice can affect the source buffer. B is incorrect: Buffer slice retains view semantics unlike TypedArray slice. C is incorrect: the important distinction is that the allocated memory is not initialized. D is correct: alloc initializes the allocated bytes. E is correct: its old memory content may otherwise leak.

sources.title: Buffer | Node.js v26.11.1 Documentation
sources.claim: Buffer.alloc zero-fills; allocUnsafe may expose old memory; Buffer.slice creates a shared-memory view; TypedArray.slice copies.

questions.prompt: A Node log helper uses `new AsyncLocalStorage()` without constructor options and calls getStore before any context is established. What does it receive?

choices.text: A newly created empty store object.
undefined
The store from the last request completed anywhere in the process.
A rejected promise whose reason contains the missing request identifier.

questions.explanation: getStore returns undefined outside an initialized context. It neither creates a default object nor retrieves another request's store.

sources.title: Asynchronous context tracking | Node.js v26.11.1 Documentation
sources.claim: AsyncLocalStorage.run propagates its store to async operations created inside the callback; an instance without a defaultValue returns undefined when no store is provided.

questions.prompt: Two ordinary Node EventEmitter listeners are registered in order and perform synchronous work. What does `emit` do?

choices.text: Queue both as microtasks instead.
Run both on worker threads and wait for their synchronous work to finish.
Call both in registration order.
Choose one listener at random so event delivery can be load balanced.

questions.explanation: EventEmitter calls listeners synchronously in registration order. A listener may separately schedule async work, but emit does not offload it automatically.

sources.title: Events | Node.js v26.11.1 Documentation
sources.claim: EventEmitter listeners execute synchronously in registration order; an unhandled error event throws and may terminate the process.

questions.prompt: A Node parser needs a private byte copy and handles potentially sensitive allocations. Which properties matter? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A Buffer.slice mutation is isolated from the source buffer by default.
Buffer.from(anExistingBuffer) copies its bytes.
Mutating a Buffer.subarray view can modify the original buffer.
An allocUnsafe buffer is safe to send before all its bytes are written.
Buffer.alloc and Buffer.allocUnsafe promise identical initialization behavior.

questions.explanation: A is incorrect: slice returns a shared view. B is correct: the buffer overload creates a separate copy. C is correct: subarray shares the same underlying memory. D is incorrect: uninitialized memory may contain sensitive previous data. E is incorrect: alloc zero-fills whereas allocUnsafe does not.

sources.title: Buffer | Node.js v26.11.1 Documentation
sources.claim: Buffer.alloc zero-fills; allocUnsafe may expose old memory; Buffer.slice creates a shared-memory view; TypedArray.slice copies.
